subtopics.title: Reading the Dashboard: Indicator Types and Timing

questions.question: Which set contains ONLY leading indicators?
options: Building plans passed, job advertisements, new vehicle sales, factory orders
Unemployment, inventories, insolvencies
Retail sales, industrial production, real GDP
The repo rate, prime, the rand

questions.question: Unemployment is classified as a lagging indicator because:
options: It is only measured once a year
Firms retrench late in a downturn and rehire cautiously in a recovery, so employment moves last
It never changes over the cycle
The survey excludes rural areas

questions.question: The difference between the LEVEL of GDP and its growth RATE is that:
options: The level is measured in dollars and the rate in rands
They are two names for the same thing
The level measures the economy's size while the rate measures its direction
The rate is always larger than the level

questions.question: Nominal GDP grew 7,5% while inflation ran 5,5%. Real growth was roughly:
options: 2,0% — nominal growth stripped of inflation

questions.question: GDP grows 0,9% while the population grows 1,5%. GDP per capita:
options: Falls — output per person shrinks even though the economy grew
Rises by 2,4%
Stays exactly constant
Cannot be affected by population growth

questions.question: The broadest money-supply aggregate, tracked by the Reserve Bank, is:
options: M1 — notes, coins and demand deposits
M3 — which adds long-term deposits to the narrower layers
M2 minus credit extension
The repo rate

questions.question: South Africa's terms of trade IMPROVE when:
options: Import volumes rise faster than export volumes
The rand weakens against the dollar
The prices of exports like platinum and coal rise relative to the prices of imports like oil and machinery
The current account moves into deficit

questions.question: The gap between the strict and expanded unemployment rates is caused by:
options: Seasonal farm work
Different provinces using different surveys
Public servants being excluded from the count
Discouraged work-seekers, counted only by the expanded definition because they have stopped searching

questions.question: Life expectancy is treated as development's summary statistic because:
options: It compresses nutrition, healthcare, clean water and safety into a single number
It is the easiest indicator to collect
It only reflects hospital quality
It never changes within a generation

questions.question: The infant mortality rate measures:
options: Deaths of children under eighteen per million people
Deaths before the first birthday per thousand live births — the sharpest poverty gauge
The number of clinics per district
Births per thousand women

questions.question: The Human Development Index blends:
options: Exports, imports and the exchange rate
Inflation, unemployment and growth
Life expectancy, education and income per person, into a score between 0 and 1
Water, sanitation and electricity coverage

questions.question: South Africa's Gini coefficient of about 0,63 indicates:
options: Moderate inequality, near the world average
Perfect equality
That 63% of citizens are unemployed
Inequality among the highest ever recorded, since 0 is perfect equality and 1 is one person holding everything

subtopics.title: Comparing Countries: PPP, Pitfalls and the Global Institutions

questions.question: China's total GDP far exceeds Switzerland's, yet the average Swiss resident is much richer. The correction that reveals this is:
options: Dividing GDP by population — comparing per capita, not totals
Converting both to euros
Adding the informal sector
Using nominal instead of real GDP

questions.question: Purchasing power parity conversion exists because:
options: Exchange rates never change
Money buys more at home in poorer countries, so market-rate conversion understates how their people actually live
Rich countries refuse to publish price data
It makes all countries' incomes equal

questions.question: Official statistics tend to OVERSTATE the gap between rich and poor countries because:
options: Poor countries inflate their numbers
Rich countries hide their production
The informal sector, subsistence farming and unpaid household work go unmeasured — and are proportionally larger in poorer countries
The World Bank rounds all figures down

questions.question: The clean separation between the IMF and the World Bank is:
options: The IMF lends to companies, the World Bank to governments
The World Bank sets exchange rates, the IMF builds dams
They are two names for one institution
The IMF provides short-term crisis finance for balance-of-payments trouble; the World Bank funds long-term development projects

questions.question: In the minibus picture, building plans and factory orders are:
options: Headlights — they promise activity next year, before the economy turns
The speedometer — they measure today's output
The rear-view mirror — they confirm the past
The fuel gauge — they measure money supply

questions.question: Jobs sit in the rear-view mirror because:
options: Employment data is collected late
Employers retrench late and rehire late, so employment always moves after the economy has turned
Unemployed people do not ride buses
Wages are set once a year

questions.question: Takings rose 7,5% while inflation ran 5,5%. The honest reading of the journey is:
options: The economy sped up by 7,5%
The economy sped up by 13%
The real advance was only about 2% — rands stretch, kilometres do not
The economy shrank by 5,5%

questions.question: South Africa's life expectancy fell sharply and then recovered by more than ten years. The recovery is explained by:
options: The rollout of antiretroviral treatment — a policy decision visible in a national statistic
Faster GDP growth
A change in how age is recorded
Emigration of older citizens

questions.question: Enrolment without learning is a weak education gauge because:
options: Schools falsify their registers
A full classroom where little is learned flatters the statistic without changing a life
Enrolment excludes private schools
Learning cannot be measured at all

questions.question: Taps, toilets and electricity are singled out as service indicators because:
options: They are the cheapest services to deliver
They never improve
They are development a household can physically touch — and about nine homes in ten now have electricity
They are excluded from the census

questions.question: The Gini coefficient asks which question of the bus?
options: How fast is the bus travelling?
How many passengers are aboard?
How far is the destination?
However much cash is on board, how is it SHARED among the passengers?

questions.question: A taxi banking R12 000 with eighteen passengers versus one banking R5 000 with three illustrates:
options: Why totals mislead — divide by the people before comparing living standards
Why bigger vehicles earn more
Why exchange rates matter
Why informal transport is untaxed

questions.question: R100 vanishes in a London café but buys a meal, a ride and airtime at home. The honest correction for this is:
options: Ignoring poor countries in comparisons
Purchasing power parity — repricing incomes by what money buys where it lives
Converting everything to dollars twice
Using the black-market exchange rate

questions.question: The vetkoek stand with no card machine and the backyard mechanic illustrate:
options: Tax evasion as a growth strategy
Why GDP should not be measured
Production the official meter never sees — which makes measured gaps between countries look wider than real ones
The superiority of formal businesses

questions.question: In 2020, South Africa borrowed about 4,3 billion dollars for pandemic relief. The lender, in its classic crisis-paramedic role, was:
options: The World Bank
The UN Development Programme
The African Development Bank
The International Monetary Fund
